title: Handling Bias in Toxic Speech Detection: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing False Positive Rates (FPR) and False Negative Rates (FNR) on text containing African-American English (AAE) dialect versus White-aligned tweets.

Measuring False Positive Equality Difference (FPED) and False Negative Equality Difference (FNED) on text containing gendered identity terms, as well as evaluating the effects of gender-swapping data augmentation.
Analyzing the combined impact of race and gender by predicting demographic associations to determine if specific intersectional groups (e.g., Black males) are disproportionately classified as toxic.
Using hand-curated template sentences to measure how toxicity predictions shift when inserting region-specific vocabulary (e.g., colloquial Indian terms versus standard English).
Evaluating model performance drops (e.g., F1 scores) on datasets augmented with non-toxic tweets from political leaders representing distinct (left-wing, right-wing, neutral) ideologies.
Calculating metrics like pinned AUC (pAUCED) and Background Positive Subgroup Negative AUC (BPSN) to evaluate spurious correlations between specific identity terms and toxicity labels.
